C-SIDEBAR-MOVE-FILE.Summary: Move files between sidebar folders by drag-and-drop, with one unified move semantics: explicit collision refusal, open-tab pathname migration, and stored table-layout / reading-position entries following the file, reusing the existing native move.
C-SIDEBAR-MOVE-FILE.Problem: The external tester cannot move a file from folder to folder in the sidebar (reported 2026-11-16). The machinery half-exists but is split and lossy: context-menu cut+paste moves the file yet leaves open tabs pointing at the dead old pathname and abandons the per-file table-layout and position stores; the only full-migration path is rename; drag-and-drop, the natural sidebar gesture, does nothing.

Goals.Goal: Dragging a file row onto a folder row (or an open root section) moves the file into that folder through the native mt_fs_move.

One project-store moveItem action owns the semantics: same-destination refusal, explicit destination-exists refusal naming the colliding file, native move, open-tab pathname/filename/DIRNAME migration, table-layouts entry migration, reading-position entry migration, tree refresh, clipboard clearing when the moved source was the clipboard.
The existing cut+paste path routes through the same action, so context-menu moves stop orphaning open tabs.
Locked or preview-only tabs do not block the move; their pathname migrates the same way.

Constraints.Constraint: No new Tauri commands, capabilities or permissions; the move reuses window.fileUtils.move (mt_fs_move).
Folder drag stays out of v1 (files only); dropping onto a file row is ignored (no implicit parent routing beyond the existing paste semantics).
Notices follow the existing sidebar paste pattern (plain English strings, no locale wave in this change).
Rename's migration behavior is the template and is not altered; the rename path keeps its own flow.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Dragging folders, cross-root moves between workspace roots, or move-on-collision renaming.
Undo of a move, trash integration, or Recent-list rewriting beyond what the existing tree refresh already does.
Localization of the new notices (follows the existing hardcoded-EN sidebar notice precedent).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Drag file → folder moves the file; drag onto the source's own folder is refused with the same-destination notice and no filesystem change.
A move whose destination already contains a same-named file is refused with a notice naming the file, before any native call.
An open tab whose file moved keeps editing the same buffer at the new pathname (tab pathname/filename updated, DIRNAME fixed for the current file) and survives save.
The stored table-layouts entry and reading-position entry for the old pathname are migrated to the new pathname on a successful move.
Cut+paste produces identical results to drag-and-drop (same action).
A failed native move leaves tabs, stores and clipboard untouched and surfaces the error notice.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Store-level unit tests with a mocked fileUtils proving both refusals, tab/store migration and failure atomicity; a source-level pin that treeFile/treeFolder wire the drag events and that SIDEBAR::paste routes through moveItem; full renderer suite green.

Assumptions.Assumption: mt_fs_move fails on an existing destination (native rename semantics), which the pre-check turns into an explicit refusal before any call.
The tree refresh after a move re-reads the directory state exactly as it does after cut+paste today.
